$comment: Reviewer registry for the review-attestation gate (GUARD-002, #906).
The gate asks ONE question: did a review actually happen? It never asks who
performed it or how good it was. A human review attests exactly as well as a
bot's.
This file exists so that answering that question does not require a code
change when the reviewer changes. #786 (TOOL-013) replaces CodeRabbit with
PR-Agent on NaN inference; that migration should be an entry below, not a
rewrite of the classifier. Building the gate BEFORE #786 is deliberate:
#786's own acceptance criterion is 'a provider failure degrading the review
rather than blocking the PR', which is the same silent green this gate
exists to end — a replacement reviewer inherits the blind spot otherwise.
`declined_markers` are the strings identifying a reviewer's 'I could not
review' notice. Matched as HTML comment markers rather than prose because
prose is translated, reworded and A/B tested, while the marker is machine
output. If a vendor changes it, the affected PR reads `pending` instead of
`declined` — still red, so marker drift degrades the MESSAGE and never the
verdict.
Note what is NOT here: any notion of which models may review. That policy
lives in harness/reviewer-pool.json and governs the SPEC-level adversarial
review, a different gate with a different purpose. The two are deliberately
not merged here — but see #786, which currently proposes qwen3.6 as a
fallback reviewer while reviewer-pool.json excludes it by name, on the
grounds that 'a reviewer that PASSes cheaply is worse than no gate'. That
contradiction needs one owner; it is flagged on #786, not decided here.

reviewers.why: Free tier, ~1 review/hour account-wide. On 2026-08-16 PRs #1007, #1009 and #1013 each carried this notice simultaneously, with zero reviews between them, while `gh pr checks` reported `CodeRabbit  pass`. Neither pushing new commits nor an explicit `@coderabbitai review` reclaims a slot while the quota is spent — measured, both.

escape.label: merged-unreviewed
escape.why: Both are required, never one. Same shape as spec-gate's skip-sdd escape, chosen because it is already understood here and because it forces the disclosure into the durable record instead of a chat message. Proceeding on an unreviewed PR is allowed; proceeding SILENTLY is not.
